rows.recovered_note: UNBLOCKING UPDATE from lead L1-API-AUTHZ, 2026-09-01. When this row was filed, its stated blocker was that Shared.Paper's grant_target_denied?/3 and all five of its helpers are defp, so the SheetGrid callsite could not share them and had to re-state the ladder over the public primitive Access.validate/3. THAT BLOCKER IS NOW PARTLY GONE. PR #14665 (pds-w42-bl-handle-info-write-seam-audit) promoted TWO of those helpers to public in api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/studio_live/shared/paper.ex — defp write_denied?/1 became def write_denied?/1, and defp refuse_write_denied/1 became def refuse_write_denied/1 — because a different seam (the {:autosave_form} handle_info write) needed to reuse the same refusal. Verified in the merged diff, not inferred. So the precedent for promoting a paper.ex predicate for cross-seam reuse now EXISTS in-tree, and whoever takes this row should check which of the remaining helpers grant_target_denied?/3 actually needs rather than assuming all five are still private. THE ONE DIFFERENCE THAT MUST SURVIVE ANY UNIFICATION, unchanged from the original filing: the paper path reloads grants fresh in handle_info, while the sheet path runs in RENDER and cannot query per render — it reads caller_context.grants and relies on the boolean short-circuit against @caps for expiry truth, so a stale set over-restricts and never under-restricts. A naive merge that gives the sheet path the paper path's fresh reload would put a query in render; one that gives the paper path the sheet path's cached read would weaken it. State which side each unified helper takes and why. ALSO NOTE the two test moduledocs in this area name symbols that do not exist (principal_chat_scope/1); do not trust moduledoc symbol names in this subtree without a grep.

rows.recovered_note: EVIDENCE APPENDIX to the close (the close itself stands; this only adds detail the 537-byte close_reason could not hold). PR #14721 merged at head ef0c0f4cd8d289f971f7f28d78621bed5aefc00d, all four required contexts SUCCESS, 42 checks 0 pending. WHAT SHIPPED: Dedup.present/1 now carries published: <bool> derived from the RAW STORED ID before norm_id/1 erases the drafts. prefix, and refusal_message/1 adds a draft-recovery note ONLY when the refusing match is draft-only. DETECTION IS BYTE-IDENTICAL BY DESIGN — draft-only rows were deliberately NOT dropped from the candidate set, because a draft-only task is still filed work and unfetching it would open a real duplicate hole to paper over a reporting one. Additive on the wire; internal/apierr's Candidate ignores unknown fields. PROOF, structural only, no timing assertion anywhere: the mechanism test (draft debris refuses a byte-identical retry at similarity 0.7, relation cross) is GREEN BEFORE the change and PINS the loop; the two reporting tests are RED before (key absent) and green after, and the published:true case stops the flag being a constant. Three mutants each red exactly the one test that owns them, tree verified clean between runs. Post-rebase on origin/main 9c7993f115: 37/0 and 81/0; content 1215/0; web controllers 1825/0; format, docs-anchors and new-lineref-check all clean. CI's never-worse ratchet 'No NEW unreachable assert messages' passed — every message-carrying assertion uses the assert x == y, 'msg' form, so the dead-message trap did not catch this change. .sobelow-annotation-bindings pins tasks/validation.ex but not tasks/dedup.ex, so a ~70-line insertion shifted no line-pinned waiver. TWO SCOPE CORRECTIONS, recorded because the scarier version circulated first: the self-poisoning is NOT progressive — attempts 2..N are refused BEFORE the insert, so exactly ONE orphan exists per (title, description) identity and lanes were not compounding their own lockout; and a PARENTED create self-excludes via the :sibling arm, so only parentless creates are exposed, which is bp task create's default. METHOD WORTH REUSING — contamination was SEPARATED from defect rather than retried away: the full suite drifted 29 -> 31 failures across two consecutive runs of an UNCHANGED tree, which is itself the shared-database signature, and CI settled it on a clean per-run Postgres. Two Plugins.Github.HealthTest failures were proven not-ours by copying origin/main's own dedup.ex over the tree, re-running health_test.exs alone to an identical 21 tests / 2 failures, then restoring and re-verifying 37/0. Same defect class as task-cffe2b5183b6ec3e (an unscoped whole-table tally asserted exactly), different module — so that row was AMENDED rather than a near-duplicate filed, verified on the PUBLISHED row at 4471 bytes with no drafts. twin stranded. Filing a duplicate would have manufactured the exact debris this PR exists to report on. UPSTREAM CAUSE, not this row: task-a0ce4e18f6776400 — fetch_candidates/2's rescue is function-wide and the DBConnection.ConnectionError is raised outside it, so the write is ambiguous and the resulting 500 gets no retry grace from transient_refusal?/1. LEDGER NOTE: my own richer close attempt returned 409 stale_claim while the row already read done — the 'errored yet wrote' shape again. Only a re-read separated 'my write failed' from 'someone else already closed it'; the closer was l2core-dedupreport at epoch 1.
